subject.title: [Feature]: Define a privacy-gated cross-platform health.summary node contract

question: Should OpenClaw support an explicitly enabled, transcript-visible `health.summary` capability as a core mobile-node feature under one shared iOS and Android contract?
rationale: Existing node invocation and authorization seams are sufficient, but accepting health aggregates into transcripts and model-provider traffic requires explicit product, privacy, retention, and mobile-store intent.

options.title: Approve bounded core contract
options.body: Freeze the minimal aggregate schema and disclosures, then implement both native readers behind in-app enablement, capability approval, and explicit Gateway allow policy.

options.title: Pilot one platform first
options.body: Validate the shared schema, consent language, and store-review posture on one native platform before committing to cross-platform parity.

options.title: Keep health outside core
options.body: Decline the native capability and leave health access to external tools or forks without an OpenClaw mobile-node contract.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded core contract
recommendation.body: Freeze the minimal aggregate schema and disclosures, then implement both native readers behind in-app enablement, capability approval, and explicit Gateway allow policy.

likelyOwner.reason: This issue is assigned to steipete, who authored the consolidation and the prior architectural decision redirecting health access through node and Gateway policy.
